ScaleDown has launched 3 small AI models for routine in-app jobs: Classify, Extract, and Summarize.

All 3 models have a 1M-token input limit, support text or images, and are accessible through ScaleDown's API, as well as OpenRouter, Vercel AI Gateway, LiteLLM, and LangChain.

> Classify - routes text by assigning user-provided labels, including a probability for each label.

> Summarize - can read long transcripts or reports and generate a short summary of up to 1,000 tokens.

note_tweet.text:
DAILY AI BRIEF 🗞 — Oct 13

META 🔥:
- Meta released Muse Wonder, its first frontier model, on the Meta Model API and in Muse Code at $4/$20 per million input/output tokens.
- Muse Wonder Full, Meta's max-reasoning variant, is launching only for Muse Code subscribers and won't be offered on the API.

SPACEXSI 🔥:
- SpaceXSI introduced The X Subscription, one set of plans covering Grok, Cursor and X Premium: Plus $8, Premium $30, Super $100 and Ultra $200 per month.

GOOGLE 🔥:
- Gemini 4 Argon is set to arrive today for Google AI Ultra subscribers.
- Antigravity CLI 1.3.4 adds Gemini 4 Argon model variants in low, medium and high.
- The Gemini app is merging its Spark agent into the main chat with new "Chat" and "Task" toggles and a "Scheduled" page.
- Google is preparing Gempix 3 Pro, likely Nano Banana 3 Pro, built on Gemini 4 Argon.
- Google launched Fitbit Edge, a $179 fitness tracker with a display and GPS, along with Google Health app updates.

ANTHROPIC 🔥:
- Claude Opus 5.5 is reportedly sometimes routing to a newer Anthropic checkpoint with stronger coding and 3D outputs.

MICROSOFT 🔥:
- Microsoft announced Maia 300, its third-gen in-house AI inference chip, rolling out to production in 2027.

OPENAI 🔥:
- Codex got another global usage-limit reset on Day 8.
- OpenAI reopened applications for its Codex Ambassador program.

NVIDIA 🔥:
- NVIDIA is opening its Vera Rubin architecture to the Open Compute Project ecosystem to help scale AI factories.

AMAZON 🔥:
- Amazon Bedrock AgentCore now has consumption-based pricing for short-term memory.

* Used Grok to compose this brief, cherry-picking the news and doing some post-editing.
